concept.name: Keltner Channel
concept.definition: Volatility envelopes around an exponential moving average, with channel lines set a multiple of Average True Range above and below the EMA; the modern version popularized by Linda Raschke replaces Chester Keltner's 1960 10-day typical-price SMA plus/minus high-low range with EMA plus/minus ATR.
concept.intuition: Like Bollinger Bands but built from ATR instead of standard deviation, Keltner Channels are smoother and more constant in width, which suits trend identification and breakout detection.
concept.mechanics: Middle line = EMA(20); upper = EMA + m x ATR(10), lower = EMA - m x ATR(10), with m = 2 by default. A close outside the channel signals extraordinary strength or weakness; a flat channel marks a range where the lines serve as overbought/oversold references.
concept.formula: Upper = EMA(P, 20) + 2 x ATR(10); Lower = EMA(P, 20) - 2 x ATR(10).
concept.failure_modes: Trend-following at heart, it lags and whipsaws in flat markets; original (SMA +/- range) and modern (EMA +/- ATR) versions differ, so values are not comparable across platforms without checking the convention.
concept.misconceptions: A close beyond the channel is not an automatic fade - it more often marks the start of a trend move than an exhaustion.
concept.example: EMA(20) = 100 and ATR(10) = 2: upper channel = 104, lower = 96; a close at 105 is an upside channel breakout.
